source.title: RMNet: Equivalently Removing Residual Connection from Networks
source.authors: Fanxu Meng; Hao Cheng; Jia-Xin Zhuang; Ke Li; Xing Sun

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares depth-dependent CIFAR accuracy for ResNet and RepVGG, and evaluates whether RM operation improves deeper RepVGG. It reports accuracy, not training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CIFAR accuracy and ImageNet accuracy, not training classification error. Figure 2 and Figure 8 values are presented as plots without numerical values in the text; cited prior results are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study uses residual networks during training and converts them to residual-free inference architectures. Its depth comparisons report accuracy, not training error, and RepVGG itself has training-time residual branches. Appendix A.2 reports better fine-tuning accuracy with BN retained but does not establish faster accuracy gains or higher learning-rate tolerance. These results do not test the named versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that RM operation removes residual connections while preserving outputs, provides favorable accuracy-speed and pruning trade-offs, and improves deeper RepVGG accuracy. These conclusions concern architecture and inference performance rather than the versions' specified optimization outcomes.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies an architectural transformation that reserves and merges features to remove residual connections, and compares accuracy and inference speed. It does not test the claim's training-error outcome.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth and reserving ratio affect RepVGG accuracy in the reported CIFAR and ImageNet comparisons; the paper describes different reserving ratios as performing better at different depths.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3 reports CIFAR-100 accuracy of 79.57% for ResNet-133 versus 41.38% for RepVGG-133. Section 5.2 reports that larger reserving ratios work better at greater depths. Neither comparison measures training error, and RepVGG has residual branches during training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth and the placement and extent of training-time residual connections affect RepVGG's classification accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix A.2 reports better accuracy when fine-tuning converted networks with BN retained rather than fused into convolutions; it does not identify a training-speed or learning-rate-tolerance effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Retaining BN improves fine-tuning accuracy after RM conversion in the tested CIFAR settings.

fits_no_version.finding: RM conversion preserves the original model's output while enabling residual-free inference; experiments evaluate inference throughput, accuracy, and pruning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RM conversion can improve inference speed and pruning trade-offs while preserving a trained residual network's function.

record.code_released: not stated; the abstract says code is available at this url, but no URL is included in the supplied text
record.problems: The relevant depth and reserving-ratio comparisons are figure-only, with no numerical values or uncertainty stated in the supplied text. Reported accuracy is not training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained because the paper reports accuracy and inference speed rather than training classification error; Figure 2, Figure 8, Tables 2 and 3, and Appendix Figure 10 therefore do not provide a row measuring the versions' named behavior.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error, including with corrupted or random labels.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their dependence on extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training error in plain versus identity-shortcut networks, longer-training controls, and the initialization exceptions.
Controlled initialization effects on learning speed, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature dynamics, and divergence.
Whether adding BN accelerates accuracy gains or permits higher learning rates; comparison with normalization-free Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: The empty row set is appropriate for these claim versions. Correct the reader's tests/T2 classification and its V3 tested_not_extracted designation. Section 3 does provide exact accuracy values, so the record's blanket statement that the depth comparisons lack numerical values is inaccurate.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, optimizer, and training duration.
Teacher-student local minima and student width relative to teacher width.

The paper examines depth-related accuracy in plain RepVGG versus ResNet and tests a method for improving deeper RepVGG, but does not report training error. The relevant accuracy outcomes cannot establish the version's training-error claim.
Initialization effects on learning speed, signal propagation, or trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability, loss dynamics, and sharpness.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed or learning-rate tolerance.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
